Water is a fundamental human need, however, this essential resource is not infinitely safe for human life. Therefore, I totally agree with the view that all governments on a global scale should have a control on the amount of clean water used in a country.

To begin with, the importance of water can be clearly seen by the fact that we as human beings cannot survive without water within three days. However, the usable resource of water must be taken into consideration as unclean or polluted water is not just dirty but it is deadly. Take some water-poor countries in Africa, the citizens there have to suffer from  plenty of deadly diseases such as diarrhea or cholera due to lack of clean water. Unfortunately, safe water is considered as a non-renewable resource.

Based on the aforementioned reasons, I think the governments should introduce stricter law relating to the use of clean water. In some countries like Vietnam, the government only encourage their residents to reduce the electricity use by asking them to pay more if they overuse the registered amount. However, this method does not seem to work well because some wealthy people do not take this into their account. Like the electricity problem, as making people pay more money on the extravagant use of water seems ineffective, the governments should limit the amount of water per capita or even cut down on the amount as a punishment.

In conclusion, because of the significance and the limit of clean water, the governments all over the world should find a way to control the citizens’ use of safe water.

Thanks to the advancement of technology, the growing popularity of remote working can be seen in many countries. It is clearly true that this trend can bring enormous benefits to companies and workers despite some of its drawbacks. My essay below will provide an analysis of both positive and negative impacts of this phenomenon.
On the downside, employees working from home are lack of face-to-face interaction with their colleagues. Although remote workers can easily attend a video conference, this communication is different from being in the office, discussing directly with co-workers. In other words, people tend to have a loss of a feeling of intimacy with their partners without regular face-to-face conversations. Therefore, teamwork spirit in a collaborative project such as achieving a collective goal is broken, reducing companies' productivity.
On the other hand, working remotely can be beneficial to both employers and employees. In terms of corporations, they can recruit any prospective employees from all over the world only by a laptop having access to the Internet. On the contrary, recruiters had to take a geographical factor into consideration when working from home was not applied. Moreover, a remote worker can gain great benefits by saving commuting time and cost. That contributes greatly to employees’ satisfaction because they can make their own choices to work in most comfortable places, then boosting their performance and work productivity.
In conclusion, with the technological development, the significant number of companies implementing remote working is on the increase. This trend is having both positive and detrimental impacts.

It is believed that the government should take responsibility for tackling childhood obesity problem due to junk foods. However, I think the responsibility should not fall upon the government alone because parents and school can make a significant contribution.
To begin with, the government should be accountable for obesity in children due to a correlation between the marketing of food and drink and this problem. To illustrate, food choices of children are usually affected by advertisement, and they tend to buy more junk food when they are constantly exposed to images of unhealthy foods on TV. If the government implement a policy on banning companies from advertising unhealthy food during children’s TV programs, children’s exposure to junk food is reduced, which leads to a positive change in children’s eating patterns. However, besides introducing new laws on advertising of junk food, I doubt that there is any further action that the government can take to tackle childhood obesity issue.
On the other hand, both parents and school can contribute to preventing obesity in children. Firstly, parents should be responsible for making all food choices on the child’s behalf until he or she can be aware of a healthy diet. If parents provide children with a balanced diet from an early age, children will have a tendency to keep this healthy habit and avoid obesity. Secondly, education about healthy diet and health threats such as obesity can provide initial support to children’s food intake. When children can have self-awareness about negative impacts of obesity such as an increased risk of chronic diseases, they will try to avoid the cause of obesity like unhealthy foods and opt for a healthy diet containing high level of nutrients.
In conclusion, I believe that the government alone cannot deal with all childhood obesity, and therefore parents and school also make a contribution to solving this problem.

Nowadays, there are more and more young people deciding to stay unmarried. The essay below will provide possible explanations for this trend and its potential impacts on the young.
To begin with, there are several reasons why the number of young people choosing to remain unmarried is increasing. Firstly, young adults tend to shift their focus from starting a stable family onto building their career. To those people, being unmarried can give them a sense of independence because they can devote much of their time and energy to what they are truly passionate about rather than taking care of a family. Secondly, young people see many celebrity couples getting divorced, leading them to lose trust in marriage. Take the Song-Song couple – a well-known Korean spouse as an example. Their marriage has lasted for only two years before ending in divorce, making their fans discouraged from getting married.
The upward trend in the number of young adults choosing not to get married can have both positive and negative effects on the young. In terms of benefits, people who decide to stay unmarried can feel more fulfilled because they have plenty of time on their own. It is proved that those people spend more time participating in voluntary work which often gives volunteers a sense of fulfillment than people who are married. Unlike married couples, although the single adults are in a long-term relationship, they may lack a complete commitment to the other. Moreover, the sense of independence may turn into the loneliness when people have to face difficulties in life on their own.
In conclusion, there are two main reasons why more and more people decide to stay unmarried. This trend can bring both benefits and drawbacks to young people.

Some people hold a belief that large public spaces such as squares and parks are a necessity for all towns and cities. While there are some disadvantages of building those facilities, I believe that their significance cannot be denied.
To begin with, it is unfeasible for all towns and cities to afford large public spaces like squares and parks because the main focus of some cities is to develop economy. In order to boost ecomony, the local authorities have to invest in building many skyscrapers for businesses and industries in cities, which takes up a great deal of space. Additionally, the need to attract more people to urban areas for economic growth purposes puts intense pressure on the housing market, therefore, authorities in those cities have to prioritize the construction of business buildings and homes rather than public spaces.
On the other hand, public spaces including squares and parks play a vital role in cities’ health. In terms of physical health, it is proved that residents living in a city with large parks or squares are less likely to catch a lifestyle disease such as obesity because they have open space to participate in many outdoor actitives on a daily basis. Regarding mental health, public spaces like squares and parks can be a get-away destination in the hustle and bustle of city life. In fact, people feel more relaxed when being immersed in a spacious and green places, which helps them release stress and prevent mental problems such as depression.
In conclusion, I believe the financial gain from converting parks or squares for economic purposes can be outweighed by the health impacts of large public places on urban residents.

The air in major cities is becoming more and more polluted, which has a detrimental effect on city
dwellers’ health. While an increasing number of personal vehicles and industrial activities can be
considered the main contributing factors to the issue, there are several feasible approaches to help
remedy it.
Firstly, high traffic volume is one of the largest sources of air pollution in urban areas. An
unprecedented number of these vehicles emit an enormous amount of exhaust fumes, such as CO2
and other hazardous gases into the atmosphere. The contaminated air is inhaled by city residents on
a daily basis, which causes many respiratory diseases such as asthma and even lung cancer. Besides,
factories that release toxic emissions into the air are often built in the vicinity of cities to cut costs of
transporting goods to consumers living there. The gases can be easily blown to towns by the wind,
and thus further complicating the problem.
Nevertheless, public transport and the relocation of factories could help improve the situation. In
order to significantly reduce the number of personal vehicles, governments should allocate more
resources to the establishment and improvement of public transport systems such as bus lines and
metro. For example, in New York City, comprehensive metro networks have been the main means of
transport for a large number of New Yorkers, which significantly eases the air pollution issue. As for
manufacturing activities, city governors should encourage companies to move their factories far from
crowded areas by offering incentives such as lower taxes or subsidized loans. The strategy can
contribute to a cleaner and healthier environment for city inhabitants.
In conclusion, a large number of motorized vehicles and manufacturing activities are the main culprits
of air pollution in large cities. Several measures mentioned above should be carefully considered and
implemented to help ensure the overall well-being of city dwellers.

People nowadays tend to use products in only a short period and then dispose of
them. This essay will discuss several contributing factors to this trend and the
problems it brings.
There are two main reasons for this consumer behavior. Firstly, breakthroughs in
technology have facilitated the mass production of goods, significantly lowering
production costs and product prices. As a result, it is easier than ever before for
consumers to dispose of their old usable items and purchase new ones with better
designs and more functions. For example, while a new television could easily cost a
thousand dollars in the 90s, in the present, one can buy one for less than 400 USD.
Furthermore, advertisements that can be seen almost everywhere, from the street
billboards to television and social platforms increasingly persuade people to make
unnecessary purchases and throw away their old products.
However, the new phenomenon has been causing serious issues. Firstly, the amount
of waste is increasing at an alarming pace due to more abandoned items. Most of
them are often transported to landfills or burnt, which pose significant threats to the
environment, including air, soil, and underwater pollution. Secondly, in order to
produce more goods to meet customers’ demand, companies have to incresingly
exploit natural resources, such as forests, oil, and metal ores. In fact, the vast
majority of these materials are limited and therefore, could be used up soon. In turn,
there will be a higher price for such depleting resources and, by extension, more
expensive consumer products in the future.
In conclusion, the availability of relatively cheaper products in the market and the
proliferation of advertising activities are considered the main culprits of people only
using goods for a short time. Unfortunately, this trend can result in the degradation
of the environment and the depletion of natural resources.

The environment indeed plays a vital part in nurturing and sustaining every life form,
including humankind, on the planet. Yet, the majority of people often do not know
much about the significance of nature. This essay will look at some reasons for this
as well as several ways to improve the situation.
There are two main contributing factors to the limited people’s understanding of the
role of nature in every aspect of their life. Firstly, in many education systems, the
main emphasis has not been on the natural world, and it is often considered trivial
compared to other subjects such as maths and physics. As a result, students are not
motivated to learn much about what the natural environment has been offering.
Secondly, there are insufficient suitable sources of information about the natural
world that are available for working people. This is mainly because entertaining
content and advertisements are becoming dominant on television and social media,
leaving people little chance to enrich their knowledge about nature.
Nevertheless, several approaches should be implemented to address the problem.
Regarding formal education, schools should prioritize extra-curriculum activities that
focus on the environment as a part of their program. For example, they can organize
regular field trips to conservation sites where students can see trees and animals and
learn about them at the same time. Besides, if governments allocate more financial
resources to programs and campaigns that focus on environmental issues, more of
them could be in the media. In this way, the general public can conveniently watch
such educational content on television or their smartphones and therefore be well-
informed of the natural world surrounding them.
In conclusion, the lack of environmental focus in school curriculum and the media
results in people being ill-informed about the environment and its roles. By
modifying the school curriculum as well as funding programs on the environment,
schools and authorities can address the problem.

Some people argue that consuming locally grown produce benefits both the
environment and the local economy. Despite its drawbacks, the merits of buying
local products are far more significant.
On the one hand, there are some disadvantages of relying on the local supply of
food. Firstly, consumers may not have a wide variety of food for their meals. This is
because local weather and climate may not be suitable for several crops; for
example, tropical countries often can not grow cherries, apples, and blueberries.
Also, some believe that a lack of competition from food grown in foreign countries
can result in local farmers becoming reluctant to improve their farming practice to
produce better products.
However, the problems can be solved. With advancements in agriculture, local
farmers have been introducing a large number of new crops on their farms, offering
a more extensive range of products to the market. Besides this, a large number of
local growers can still ensure a certain extent of competition, which drives them to
continually enhancing their product’s quality while keeping the price affordable.
On the other hand, the environmental and economic gains from favoring local
produce are remarkable. Consuming food grown on closeby farmland is
environmentally friendly. Local produce travels a much shorter distance from farm to
table, so much less greenhouse gas is released into the atmosphere compared to its
foreign counterpart. Furthermore, the trend helps develop the local economy. If
farmers earn more income from selling products to local residents, they can invest
and expand their business, which leads to more locals being employed and higher
economic growth. Thus, there is a lot to be gained when people support produce
from their community.
In conclusion, the main disadvantages of buying locally grown food relate to
relatively higher prices and fewer choices. Nevertheless, the environmental and
economic benefits of the preference eclipse its downsides.

Governments have been using technologies to track citizens’ speech and behavior, in some cases,
without their awareness. While the practice comes with some drawbacks, its merits are far more
significant.
There are two main problems that monitoring people can bring. Firstly, many people concern that
they may lose their freedom. This is because privacy is one of the fundamental human rights.
Therefore, it is hard to accept that one’s private calls, travels, and acts are constantly tracked by
governmental officials. Furthermore, if used indiscriminately, some governments may take advantage
of this type of surveillance to take total control over its residents. For example, in North Korea, people
who escaped from the country often report that they afraid of being charged heavy sentences for
their speech or thoughts that may be against the rulers’ wishes. Thus, this type of surveillance may
lead to people becoming reluctant to express their opinions and feeling oppressed.
On the other hand, monitoring activities can bring tremendous benefits. By tracking people’s
communication and activities, law enforcement agencies can gain invaluable information to find and
attack terrorist and criminal organizations. In fact, there have been many cases in which police
successfully tracked criminal’s phone calls or emails and managed to stopped the potential crimes,
ensuring safety for every citizen. Furthermore, a high safety level facilitates economic development.
Investors and enterprises are more likely to invest in safe countries where terrorism and criminal
activities are under control, thus creating more jobs and resulting in higher economic growth. Hence,
the increased level of safety brought about is of great benefit to only individuals but also society as a
whole.
In conclusion, the main disadvantages of civil censorship relate to personal privacy and dictatorships.
However, the benefits of this policy more than make up for any potential drawbacks.

The world today witnesses the drastic changes in the way people reorganise their life. While
some not only successfully handle the work requirements, but also continuously enjoy life
comfort, others are still out of control of what they are trying to obtain. Consequently, they
constantly face countless detrimental impacts and this leads to a range of unexpected issues.
To demonstrate the negative effects on people’s life regarding the aforementioned problem,
these are some undeniable drawbacks. Some people who are regarded as workaholics and are
always flooded with work hardly arrange their time for recreational activities, this truly causes
them under an excessive amount of stress and soon ruins both their physical and mental
health. On the contrary, those who undermine the importance of work and devote too much
time to other purposes rather than jobs and careers would suffer from the financial crisis
because their spending exceeds their incomes.
Unquestionably, the problems mentioned above are surprisingly rising at an alarming rate and
useful solutions seem to be prerequisites to weaken these predictable sequences. People
themselves desperately need to raise the awareness of the importance of life working
balancing through courses which specifically specialise in time management and provide them
with the necessary skills to effectively allocate their time and budgets. Besides, companies’ top
leaders should delegate tasks to their employees more equally and more suitably so that they
could have time to fulfill other individual needs.
In conclusion, it is indispensable for individuals to keep their pace of life. There are still so many
obstacles arising and that requires people to find out ways to make their life more well-
organised.

Nowadays, individuals all over the world find it hard to spend time with other family members.
Obviously, this has caused countless issues which will be argued in the following parts. In
addition, some reasons leading to this reality will also be included.
It is universally believed that the issue mentioned above might come from all members living
under the same roof. First of all, most parents who are breadwinners have to suffer from an
excessive amount of pressure because of their heavy workloads. They devote nearly all of their
time to work so that cannot find sufficient time for their children. Secondly, in this modern
world, children themselves are pursuiting their own living lifestyles which are featured by the
tendency of living independently and doing things without parental supervision.
The lack of time for family connections truly causes many negative impacts, first and foremost,
on each member of a family and even the society. This matter will directly decrease the family
bond which consequently leads to the shortage of close-knit relationships among members.
Kids and teenagers may not receive necessary attention from their parents and may be
educated inappropiately. In terms of society, the continuation of this situation in a long time,
sooner or later, can spoil the nucleus values of family traditions which have been passed down
from early generations. For example, in the past, there used to be many extended families
where three or more generations live in harmony. However, the popularity of nuclear families is
surprisingly increasing and this type of family accounts for a greater proportion than it used to
be.
In conclusion, people individually should take this matter into serious consideration. With some
convincing reasons argued, people must take actions promptly in order to prevent the
aforementioned problems.
